newsitem.title: USA: Glickman says access key to Chile joining NAFTA.
newsitem.headline: Glickman says access key to Chile joining NAFTA.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday that he supports Chile joining NAFTA and reauthorizing fast-track authority to the president, but said that some agricultural trade access issues with Chile need to be resolved.

Testifying before the House Appopriations subcommittee on Agriculture and Rural Development, Glickman said he met with Chilean President Eduardo Frei earlier Wednesday during Frei's visit to Washington.

Glickman said he and Frei briefly discussed trade issues, and that Chile and the United States have agreed to begin a consultative process to discuss Chile's import restrictions on U.S. wheat, poultry and fresh fruits and vegetables.
"It is clear that agricultural issues have to be worked out ... (but) it is our desire to move ahead with fast-track," he said.

At a news conference Wednesday, Frei said bilateral trade with the United States had undergone an explosive increase and there were sensitive issues between the two countries, "especially in agricultural sectors."

Glickman said he will go to Chile sometime in May to discuss pending issues. He said Chile, for example, is putting strict regulations on the karnal bunt wheat fungus that no other country in the world has implemented. "We need to get these removed," he said.

Glickman told lawmakers that increasing U.S. agricultural exports will be the "ultimate safety net" for American farmers under the new U.S. farm bill. The bill sharply reduced most federal support programs to farmers.
"Exports and trade opportunites are the best things we can do to keep agriculture strong," he said.

He said that USDA is asking for full funding for the Export Enhancement Program in its 1998 budget proposals in order to be ready to fight unfair trade practices, but said he did not want to "have to go down that road" of export subsidies if he could help it.
